outcome: Since 26 Jan 2024 one sole-author arXiv preprint claims a full proof of the characteristic-0 statement (Ghosh, arXiv:2501.09272, posted 16 Jan 2025, revised 21 Mar 2026). I found no journal record, referee report, formal check or published error report for it, and a 12 Aug 2026 paper says it has not been independently verified and treats the conjecture as open. The other in-window events are partial results: a dimension bound, a conditional bound on bad primes, and obstructions on hypothetical counterexamples.
problem_asks: Statement: let f be a polynomial of degree d over a field K of characteristic 0 such that, for each i = 1, ..., d-1, f has a nonconstant common factor with its i-th derivative (one factor per derivative; the factor need not be the same for each). Question: must f be the d-th power of a linear polynomial, i.e. f = c(X-alpha)^d with c and alpha in K? Parts asked: (a) the implication for every degree d (the nontrivial range is d >= 3; d = 1 is vacuous and d = 2 is elementary); (b) for every field K of characteristic 0, not only C or algebraically closed fields; (c) the conclusion in the form of a d-th power of a linear polynomial over K itself. The converse (a d-th power satisfies the hypothesis) is not asked and holds in characteristic 0. Wikipedia words the bullet as a question ('must f be ...?'); the conjecture is that the implication holds.

events.what_happened: Second-hand only. A lecture-slide deck by Duong (pub.math.leidenuniv.nl/~edixhovensj/tag_2009/duong_2.pdf, seen as a search snippet and not opened) reports a 'simple proof' of the conjecture by Peter Ullrich in 2005, which the author withdrew because its main proof was wrong. I did not find the arXiv listing and cannot confirm its version history, title or exact date.
events.delivers: Claimed a full proof of the conjecture (as reported second-hand). Withdrawn, so it establishes nothing.
events.remains: All of problem_asks, given the withdrawal.
events.doubts: The slide deck says the main proof was wrong (second-hand; the deck itself was not opened).

withdrawn.what: Claimed simple proof, withdrawn because the main proof is wrong (per Duong's slides, second-hand)

events.direction: Claims the conjecture is true (cuts toward the conjecture); withdrawn.

events.what_happened: Giulia Battiston posted 'The Casas-Alvero conjecture' (arXiv:1511.04932) on 16 Nov 2015. The abstract says the paper presents a proof of the conjecture for complex polynomials (a root in common with each derivative forces a power of a linear factor). Version 2 (19 Nov 2015) is withdrawn: 'The paper has been withdrawn as it contains a crucial error in its last page, I am thankful to Joseph Schicho for pointing it out to me.' The v2 page has no PDF. I did not open the v1 PDF.
events.revisions: v1 16 Nov 2015 (claimed proof); v2 19 Nov 2015 withdrawn for a crucial error on the last page.
events.delivers: A claimed proof over C that a complex polynomial sharing a root with each derivative is a power of a linear polynomial. Withdrawn, so it establishes nothing.
events.remains: All of problem_asks, given the withdrawal.

checked_by.qualification: Co-author of Graf von Bothmer, Labs, Schicho and van de Woestijne (J. Algebra 2007), the main published characteristic-0 result on this conjecture (author list checked on arXiv:math/0605090)
checked_by.what_they_did: Found a crucial error on the last page, as the author's withdrawal comment credits him

events.doubts: Withdrawn for a crucial error on the last page; the comment does not say what the error is or whether the main argument is affected.

withdrawn.what: v2 withdrawn: crucial error on the last page, credited to Joseph Schicho

events.direction: Claimed proof of the conjecture (cuts toward the conjecture); withdrawn.
people: Joseph Schicho (credited with finding the error)

events.what_happened: Luis J. Fernandez de las Heras and Maria J. Fernandez de las Heras posted 'Three proofs of the Casas-Alvero conjecture' (arXiv:1306.5656, 19 Jun 2013, math.GM). The abstract says the conjecture concerns interpolation polynomials, that partial proofs exist but none in the general case, and that the authors propose three proofs. The rendered abstract has one broken link that the fetch tool filled in. The abstract does not say which degrees or fields the three proofs cover. I did not read the body.
events.delivers: Claims three proofs. Their scope is not stated in the abstract, so I cannot say what they establish; the abstract itself says the general case was not proven before them.
events.remains: Unknown without the body; possibly all of problem_asks.
events.doubts: Scope of the claimed proofs is not stated in the abstract. No public engagement found in my searches. The body was not read.
events.direction: Claims proofs of the conjecture (cuts toward the conjecture); scope unclear.
people: Luis J. Fernandez de las Heras
Maria J. Fernandez de las Heras

events.what_happened: Edward Dobrowolski posted 'Casas-Alvero Conjecture is true' (arXiv:1705.01704) on 4 May 2017. The abstract reads: 'The article presents the proof of Casas-Alvero conjecture.' Version 2 (7 May 2017) is withdrawn. The comments field says: 'Jacob Tsimerman found an irreparable error in the proof'. The author affiliation (University of Northern British Columbia) comes from a search snippet of the PDF, not from the abstract page. I did not read the v1 body.

events.remains: All of problem_asks, given the withdrawal.

checked_by.qualification: Named in the arXiv comments field as the person who found the error; I did not verify his standing in this session
checked_by.what_they_did: Reported an irreparable error in the proof (per the comments field)

people: Jacob Tsimerman (named as finding the error)

events.what_happened: Zhipeng Lu posted 'Casas-Alvero conjecture in computational algebraic geometry' (arXiv:1707.04754, v1 15 Jul 2017). The current abstract (v6, 16 Mar 2021) says the paper studies varieties parametrising polynomials of derivatives, using Combinatorial Nullstellensatz and Noether normalisation, shows the polynomials form regular sequences, and 'consequently give a proof to the Casas-Alvero conjecture' (verbatim). Version 3 (26 Mar 2018) is marked withdrawn, with no reason on the abstract page. Search snippets (not opened) report a withdrawn-version comment about serious gaps, and a 'tentative' label in a later version, and an introduction that still calls the conjecture unproven. I could not verify these snippets.
events.revisions: v1 15 Jul 2017; v2 24 Jul 2017; v3 26 Mar 2018 withdrawn; v4 27 Jul 2018; v5 14 Nov 2019; v6 16 Mar 2021 (current).
events.delivers: Claims the full conjecture (no field or degree restriction in the abstract) by a dimension computation for parametrised polynomial varieties. Whether the claim is intended for all characteristic-0 fields is not stated in the abstract.
events.remains: Nothing, if the claim held. The argument has not been checked by me or by any source I found.
events.time_since_posted: about 9 years (v1 2017; claim still in v6, 2021)
events.doubts: v3 withdrawn with no reason on the abstract page. The abstract's proof claim conflicts with the 'tentative' and 'still unproven' wording reported in snippets (not verified). No public engagement found.

withdrawn.what: v3 marked withdrawn; no reason shown on the abstract page
withdrawn.by: unknown (not stated on the abstract page)

events.direction: Claimed proof of the conjecture (cuts toward the conjecture).

events.what_happened: Hans-Christian Graf von Bothmer, Oliver Labs, Josef Schicho and Christiaan van de Woestijne posted 'The Casas-Alvero conjecture for infinitely many degrees' (arXiv:math/0605090, v1 3 May 2006; v2 25 Jun 2007). Published in J. Algebra 316(1) (2007), 224-230. The abstract says that over characteristic 0 the conjecture holds when the degree is a prime power or twice one, and that for every positive characteristic p there are counterexamples.
events.revisions: v1 3 May 2006; v2 25 Jun 2007 (typos, references, computational section); journal version J. Algebra 316(1) 2007.
events.delivers: Characteristic 0, degree d = p^k or 2p^k (p prime, k >= 1). Restricted to those degrees; other degrees are not covered.
events.remains: Every other degree (for example 12, 20, 24, 28), so the statement in full.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in J. Algebra 316(1), 2007, pp. 224-230 (journal reference on the arXiv page)

events.direction: Proves the statement for the restricted degrees in characteristic 0 (cuts toward the conjecture). Shows the characteristic-0 hypothesis is essential by positive-characteristic counterexamples.
events.object: In every positive characteristic p there is a polynomial of some degree that is not a d-th power yet shares a factor with each of its first d-1 derivatives (for example X^(p+1) - X^p, and any g(X^p)). These are explicit counterexamples in characteristic p, not in characteristic 0.

events.what_happened: Wouter Castryck, Robert Laterveer and Myriam Ounais posted 'Constraints on counterexamples to the Casas-Alvero conjecture, and a verification in degree 12' (arXiv:1208.5404, 27 Aug 2012, one version). The abstract says 'we settle the Casas-Alvero conjecture in degree 12', combining theoretical constraints on counterexamples with an improved Groebner basis method (building on Diaz-Toca and Gonzalez-Vega), and extends the Graf von Bothmer et al. proof to the families 5p^k, 6p^k and 7p^k with listed exceptional primes. The computer algebra software is not named in the abstract. A journal version (possibly Math. Comp. 2014) appeared in a search result and was not opened.
events.delivers: Characteristic 0, degree 12 (by a computation combined with theory), plus the 5p^k, 6p^k and 7p^k families with the listed exceptions. Computer-based, not a human-only argument.
events.remains: All other degrees, including 20, 24 and 28; the statement in full.
events.doubts: I did not confirm the journal publication or any independent check of the degree-12 computation. The degree-12 claim rests on a computation whose code I did not inspect.
events.direction: Settles one degree and extends families in characteristic 0 (cuts toward the conjecture for those degrees).

events.what_happened: Semyon Yakubovich posted 'Polynomial problems of the Casas-Alvero type' (arXiv:1308.5320; v1 24 Aug 2013; v2 withdrawn 28 Aug 2013; v5 13 Dec 2019). The abstract gives necessary and sufficient conditions for a polynomial to be trivial (of the form a(x-b)^n), root bounds and Abel-Goncharov identities, and says the results are applied to the Casas-Alvero problem. The body describes investigating 'particular cases of the problem' where the conjecture may hold or may be false. It does not claim to settle any case.
events.revisions: v1 24 Aug 2013; v2 28 Aug 2013 withdrawn; v3 30 Aug 2013; v4 30 Oct 2013; v5 13 Dec 2019.
events.delivers: Root-property and inequality results for polynomials; no case of the conjecture is stated to be settled. Discounted as a related-problem result.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.direction: Partial and tangential; does not say which way the conjecture goes.

events.what_happened: Semyon Yakubovich posted 'Towards the Casas-Alvero conjecture' (arXiv:1504.00274; v1 1 Apr 2015; v2 14 Aug 2015). The abstract gives necessary and sufficient conditions for triviality of a degree-n polynomial, a determinantal representation of Abel-Goncharov interpolation polynomials, and Sz.-Nagy-type identities. It is framed as progress toward the conjecture over C, and claims no degree resolved.
events.delivers: Identities and conditions toward the conjecture over C; no degree or case stated as settled.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.direction: Partial and tangential; does not say which way the conjecture goes.

events.what_happened: Second-hand only. Jan Draisma and Johan P. de Jong, 'On the Casas-Alvero conjecture', EMS Newsletter 80 (2011), 29-33, a survey. Search snippets (not opened) say it uses the Gauss-Lucas theorem to prove the conjecture for degrees up to 4 and list 12, 20, 24 and 28 as the smallest open cases at the time.
events.delivers: Degrees up to 4 (second-hand); a survey of the state of the problem in 2011.
events.remains: All degrees above 4 in the second-hand summary.
events.doubts: Second-hand; the survey was not opened.
events.direction: Partial results toward the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Cesar Massri posted arXiv:1806.09561 on 25 Jun 2018. Per a search snippet, v1 was titled 'The Casas-Alvero Conjecture is true' (v1 body not read). Versions 2, 3 and 5 are withdrawn (26 Jun 2018, 9 Oct 2019, 12 Jan 2022). Version 4 (20 Dec 2021) and version 6 (25 Aug 2023) are active. Current v6, titled 'The Casas-Alvero conjecture for three recycled roots in degree 20', abstract: the number of possible counterexamples in normal form of degree p^r+p^s or p^r+2p^s is finite; a possible counterexample in normal form of degree p^r+1 has algebraic coefficients; 'in degree 20 there are no counterexamples with three recycled roots'. No withdrawal reason is shown.
events.revisions: v1 25 Jun 2018 (title per snippet, claimed proof); v2 26 Jun 2018 withdrawn; v3 9 Oct 2019 withdrawn; v4 20 Dec 2021; v5 12 Jan 2022 withdrawn; v6 25 Aug 2023 (current, partial results).
events.delivers: v6: finiteness of counterexample normal forms in degrees p^r+p^s and p^r+2p^s; algebraic coefficients for p^r+1; no counterexample of degree 20 with three recycled roots. These are restricted classes and do not settle the conjecture.
events.remains: The conjecture in full; degree 20 in general (counterexamples with other root patterns are not ruled out by v6); all degrees outside the stated families.
events.doubts: Earlier versions carried the full claim and were withdrawn (v2, v3, v5), with no reasons shown. The v1 body, and the content of the withdrawn versions, were not read.

withdrawn.what: v2, v3 and v5 withdrawn; no reason shown; v1 carried the title 'The Casas-Alvero Conjecture is true' (per snippet)

events.direction: Partial results: restricted classes of possible counterexamples are finite or constrained (cuts toward the conjecture in those classes); the full statement is not settled.

events.what_happened: Daniel Schaub (LAREMA) and Mark Spivakovsky (IMT), 'On the set of bad primes in the study of Casas-Alvero Conjecture' (arXiv:2307.05997; v1 12 Jul 2023; v2 22 Aug 2023). The abstract gives a strategy (verify in a small degree d, list bad primes for d, extend to degrees d*p^l for good primes p) and computes distinguished monomials in the resultants R(f, H_i(f)) to produce a non-exhaustive list of bad primes in every degree.
events.delivers: Non-exhaustive lists of bad primes for every degree; settles no case of the conjecture.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.direction: Tool for the strategy; does not say which way the conjecture goes.

events.what_happened: Daniel Schaub and Mark Spivakovsky, 'A note on the Casas-Alvero Conjecture' (arXiv:2312.08742). v1 14 Dec 2023; v2 13 Nov 2024; v3-v7 5-11 Feb 2025. The v7 main result: for i in {d-3, d-2, d-1}, the resultant R_i does not lie in the radical of the ideal generated by the other resultants R_j (j not equal to i). It is presented as a very partial step toward the conjecture's expected independence of resultants. The v7 text carries an 'Added in press' note after Theorem 5 (quoted in the next event). I did not check whether v1 already contains the R_i result.
events.revisions: v1 14 Dec 2023; v2 13 Nov 2024; v3 5 Feb 2025; v4 6 Feb 2025; v5 7 Feb 2025; v6 10 Feb 2025; v7 11 Feb 2025. The result's first appearance may be a later version than v1; v1 content not checked.
events.delivers: A partial step: R_i (i in {d-3, d-2, d-1}) is not in the radical of the ideal of the other resultants. No degree is settled, and no proof of the conjecture is claimed by these authors.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.direction: Partial, toward the conjecture; does not say which way it goes.

events.what_happened: In the 2025 revision history of arXiv:2312.08742 (versions dated 5-11 Feb 2025), the authors add an 'Added in press' note after Theorem 5, which reads: 'In two recent preprints [6] and [7] Soham Ghosh gave a complete proof of the Casas-Alvero conjecture.' [6] is arXiv:2402.18717 and [7] is arXiv:2501.09272. The note does not describe any checking of the argument. I did not establish which version first carries the note; it is in the v7 text I read.
events.revisions: Note present in the v7 text (11 Feb 2025 version); exact first version carrying it not established.
events.delivers: A statement by two specialists that Ghosh's two preprints give a complete proof. Not a verification, and the authors claim no proof of their own.
events.remains: Nothing beyond what the endorsement claims; no independent check is described.

checked_by.qualification: Specialists who have written three arXiv papers on this conjecture (2307.05997, 2312.08742, 2411.13967)
checked_by.what_they_did: Cited the two Ghosh preprints in a note as giving a complete proof; the note describes no checking of the argument

events.time_since_posted: about 20 months after the Ghosh preprint
events.doubts: Spivakovsky is thanked in Ghosh's acknowledgements for carefully reading several drafts of the paper (Ghosh v2 HTML), so this endorsement is not independent of the author. The note describes no verification.
events.direction: Endorsement of the characteristic-0 claim (cuts toward the conjecture as proved), by non-independent specialists.

events.what_happened: Soham Ghosh posted arXiv:2402.18717 on 28 Feb 2024 (v2 18 Sep 2024; v3 14 Jan 2025, comment 'Section 6 on intermediate Casas-Alvero schemes added. Submitted version'). The current title is 'A finiteness result towards the Casas-Alvero Conjecture'. A search snippet gives the v1 title as 'Finiteness of the Arithmetic Casas-Alvero Scheme' (not verified on the abstract page). The abstract says that over any algebraically closed field of any characteristic the variety of such polynomials has dimension at most two for every positive degree, so the arithmetic scheme has finitely many rational points over any field; it also proves rigidity results and introduces intermediate schemes. For fixed degree the abstract says the conjecture is equivalent to that variety being one-dimensional. The abstract does not claim the conjecture is proved.
events.revisions: v1 28 Feb 2024; v2 18 Sep 2024; v3 14 Jan 2025 (current).
events.delivers: Dimension at most two for the variety of such polynomials (algebraically closed fields, any characteristic), and finiteness of rational points of the arithmetic scheme. This is a bound, not the one-dimensionality that the conjecture needs in each degree.
events.remains: Whether the variety is one-dimensional in each degree, which is the conjecture's content in each degree, in characteristic 0.
events.direction: Partial: a dimension bound that moves toward the conjecture without reaching it.

events.what_happened: Daniel Schaub and Mark Spivakovsky posted arXiv:2411.13967 on 21 Nov 2024 (one version). The abstract gives an explicit description of the bad primes in any degree n and an explicit upper bound for them, which holds if the conjecture holds in degree n. The comments field reads 'arXiv admin note: text overlap with arXiv:2307.05997'. The abstract does not claim the conjecture in any degree and does not mention degree 20.
events.delivers: A conditional bound: if the conjecture holds in degree n, the bad primes for n are bounded by an explicit expression in n. No degree is settled.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.direction: Conditional, technical; does not say which way the conjecture goes.

events.what_happened: Soham Ghosh, 'Proof of the Casas-Alvero conjecture', arXiv:2501.09272 (sole author, math.AC and math.AG). v1 16 Jan 2025; v2 21 Mar 2026 (comment: 'Major revisions'). Theorem A, as stated in the v1 HTML: for a monic univariate polynomial f of degree d >= 3 over a characteristic-zero field K, gcd(f, f_i) is nontrivial for each i = 1..d-1 if and only if f = (X-alpha)^d for some alpha in K. The v2 abstract adds that the proof uses Koszul homology and that the paper also constructs 'almost counterexamples' over C with Brouwer degree techniques. The v1 proof sketch says 'Without loss of generality we will assume our fields to be algebraically closed' and states Proposition A, on which the proof relies, for algebraically closed fields. In v2 the injectivity step (Proposition 4.3) is stated under the hypothesis that the characteristic of K is 0; the introduction calls the induced map on 0th Koszul homology injective. A model paraphrase of the v2 PDF says the minimal-generator step 'works only over C'; I could not confirm that sentence in the text I read. The v2 bibliography and the full Section 4 argument were not read.
events.revisions: v1 16 Jan 2025; v2 21 Mar 2026 with comment 'Major revisions'. What changed between v1 and v2 is not established.
events.delivers: As claimed: the full characteristic-0 statement for every d >= 3 and every characteristic-0 field K (d = 1, 2 elementary). No restriction beyond characteristic 0 is stated in Theorem A; the v1 reduction to algebraically closed fields is asserted without the justification I could read.
events.remains: Nothing, if the proof is correct. Unverified: no journal, referee report, formal check or published error report found, and a 12 Aug 2026 paper treats the conjecture as open because the proof 'has not been independently verified'.

checked_by.qualification: Specialists on this conjecture; Spivakovsky is also thanked in the paper's acknowledgements for reading drafts
checked_by.what_they_did: Cited the preprint in an 'Added in press' note as giving a complete proof; the note describes no checking

events.doubts: (1) No journal record, referee report, expert write-up, Lean/Coq check or error report found. (2) The only public endorsement is by co-authors, one of whom is thanked in the acknowledgements for reading drafts. (3) Marashdeh (12 Aug 2026) states that 'as that work has not been independently verified, the conjecture is treated here as open'. (4) Scope tension: the v1 reduction to algebraically closed fields, and Proposition A stated only for algebraically closed fields, against Theorem A's any-characteristic-0-field claim; the v2 'works only over C' phrase is unconfirmed. For the judging pass: in characteristic 0, a monic (X-alpha)^d over the algebraic closure has alpha = -a_(d-1)/d in K, and gcd(f, f_i) is the same over K and over its closure, so the reduction looks routine (this is my inference, not checked against the paper). (5) The v2 revision ('Major revisions', 2026) content is unknown. (6) Four earlier claimed proofs of the same statement were withdrawn (Battiston 2015, Dobrowolski 2017, Lu 2017 partly, Massri 2018 partly); this is history, not a specific error in this paper.
events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture: asserts that every such f of degree d >= 3 over any characteristic-0 field is a d-th power of a linear polynomial.
events.object: No counterexample is exhibited. The paper constructs 'almost counterexamples' over C, polynomials that satisfy somewhat weaker hypotheses than the conjecture's, using Brouwer degree techniques (v2 abstract). Their precise statement was not read.

events.what_happened: Soham Ghosh gave the UW Student AG Seminar talk 'On the Casas-Alvero conjecture' (Thu 17 Apr 2025, 3-4 pm, PDL C-401). The abstract says the talk shows that over any field of characteristic p > 0 there are 'finitely many' counterexamples, 'will also sketch a proof' of the characteristic-0 conjecture, and gives a corollary that rational normal curves are set-theoretic complete intersections in characteristic 0. It says the talk is based on arXiv:2402.18717 and arXiv:2501.09272.
events.delivers: A sketch of the characteristic-0 argument already posted in 2501.09272, and finiteness of counterexamples in characteristic p > 0 (as claimed). No new written argument. Discounted as a restatement by the author.
events.doubts: The talk is given by the author; it is not an independent engagement.
events.direction: As for 2501.09272 (characteristic 0 claimed as a sketch).

events.what_happened: University of Washington Mathematics news item (posted 20 Aug 2025 by Rose Choi) on Ghosh being one of the first Simons Dissertation Fellows in mathematics. It credits 'his recent resolution of the Casas-Alvero conjecture', and the word 'resolution' links to arXiv:2501.09272.
events.delivers: An institutional description of the 2501.09272 work as a resolution. Not a check of the argument; the item does not say whether the work is published or peer-reviewed. Discounted.
events.doubts: Institutional praise, not a mathematical check.
events.direction: Describes the 2501.09272 claim as a resolution (cuts toward the conjecture as proved).

events.what_happened: Mohammad F. Marashdeh, 'A descent-set obstruction for the Casas-Alvero conjecture', arXiv:2608.14726 (v1 12 Aug 2026; math.NT, one version). Main result (Theorem 5): for each i in {d-3, d-2, d-1}, R_i does not lie in the radical of the ideal of the other resultants. Other results: stratification by the support of centred normal forms; when one root suffices, the remaining count is MacMahon's determinant (permutations with a given descent set); no counterexample needs fewer than three recycled roots; bad primes in characteristic p (691 in degree 11); no two-element support in characteristic zero; a counterexample needs at least four terms in centred normal form. On the Ghosh preprint, the paper says: 'A proof of Conjecture 1.1 in full generality is announced in a preprint of S. Ghosh [10], by means of Koszul homology; as that work has not been independently verified, the conjecture is treated here as open.' It adds: 'Neither reduction proves the conjecture.'
events.delivers: Obstructions and partial results in characteristic 0 (no counterexample with fewer than three recycled roots; no two-element supports; at least four terms in centred normal form) and characteristic-p bad primes. It settles no case of the conjecture.
events.remains: The conjecture in full. The author treats it as open and does not rely on the Ghosh proof.
events.doubts: None on this paper's own results. It is a later paper that does not treat 2501.09272 as established.
events.direction: Obstructions that rule out some shapes of counterexample, consistent with the conjecture being true; does not settle it either way.

disputes.summary: Wikipedia (last edited 13 Aug 2026) still calls d = 20 the smallest open degree and mentions no 2025 claim. Schaub and Spivakovsky (Feb 2025 'Added in press' note) say Ghosh 'gave a complete proof'. Marashdeh (12 Aug 2026) says the proof 'has not been independently verified' and treats the conjecture as open. I did not resolve this, and it is recorded for the judging pass.

Lu (arXiv:1707.04754): the current abstract says the paper gives a proof of the conjecture, while snippets (not opened) report that the introduction of some version still calls the conjecture unproven and that an earlier version called the argument tentative. I could not verify these snippets.

summary: Sources: arXiv abstract pages for every event below, the arXiv HTML for Ghosh's two versions and for the Schaub-Spivakovsky v7 and Marashdeh papers, the Wikipedia article, and two UW pages. Where a PDF returned only compressed bytes, I used the HTML rendering, and where an HTML page was longer than the fetch window, I read the parts available and say so. What happened: the only event since 26 Jan 2024 that claims the full characteristic-0 statement is Ghosh's arXiv:2501.09272 (v1 16 Jan 2025, sole author, Koszul homology; v2 21 Mar 2026, 'Major revisions'). Its public uptake is: an 'Added in press' endorsement in the Feb 2025 revisions of Schaub and Spivakovsky's note (arXiv:2312.08742), from co-authors one of whom Ghosh thanks for reading drafts; Ghosh's own UW talk of 17 Apr 2025, which sketches the proof; a UW news item of 20 Aug 2025 calling it a 'resolution'; and Marashdeh's arXiv:2608.14726 (12 Aug 2026), which says the proof 'has not been independently verified' and treats the conjecture as open. I found no journal acceptance, referee report, Lean or Coq formalisation, expert write-up or published error report for 2501.09272. The other in-window events are partial: Ghosh's dimension bound (arXiv:2402.18717, 28 Feb 2024; bound two, while the conjecture needs one), Schaub-Spivakovsky's conditional bound on bad primes (arXiv:2411.13967, 21 Nov 2024), the R_i step in arXiv:2312.08742 (first posted Dec 2023, revised Feb 2025), and Marashdeh's obstructions. Pre-window history is a run of claimed full proofs that were withdrawn (Battiston 2015, with a crucial error pointed out by Schicho; Dobrowolski 2017, with an irreparable error reported by Tsimerman per the arXiv comments; Lu 2017, with its v3 withdrawn; Massri 2018, with several versions withdrawn) and a second-hand Ullrich 2005 claim. The established restricted results are Graf von Bothmer, Labs, Schicho and van de Woestijne (J. Algebra 2007: degrees p^k and 2p^k) and Castryck, Laterveer and Ounais (2012: degree 12, computer-assisted, and families 5p^k, 6p^k, 7p^k). Close calls: (a) whether Ghosh's argument is correct, which I could not check beyond the parts of the HTML I read; (b) scope: Theorem A claims every characteristic-0 field, but the v1 proof sketch assumes algebraically closed fields and the v2 HTML states its injectivity step only under 'characteristic 0'; a model paraphrase of the v2 PDF also says one step 'works only over C', which I could not confirm in the text I read; (c) whether the Schaub-Spivakovsky endorsement counts as a human check, given that it describes no checking and that Spivakovsky read drafts. AI: no source I read names an AI system for any event, including the acknowledgements of Ghosh's paper (which thank Spivakovsky and cite NSF grants). Moonlight's machine-generated review pages describe the Ghosh paper as an AI-written proof summary; those are not sources about how the mathematics was done, and I did not open them (rate-limited). I searched for OpenAI, DeepMind, Anthropic and Epoch AI links to the conjecture and found none, and the AI-solved results I saw concern other problems (Sendov, Jacobian, Erdos problems) and are not recorded here.
competing_reading: The case that Ghosh's paper resolves the characteristic-0 statement: it is a complete, structured sole-author proof with an explicit theorem and a clear main step; two specialists have cited it in print as giving a complete proof; the author has presented it at UW and it has been recognised by the university; and Marashdeh's 'not independently verified' is a neutral description of the absence of referee review, not a finding of error. The reduction to algebraically closed fields looks routine (see the Ghosh event). Against this: the only endorsement comes from co-authors, one of whom read drafts; nothing has been refereed or formally checked in 21 months; five earlier claims of the same statement were withdrawn after errors; and the v1 text states its key proposition only over algebraically closed fields while the theorem claims any characteristic-0 field.
what_would_settle_it: A journal acceptance or referee report for arXiv:2501.09272; an expert write-up or Lean/Coq formalisation of Proposition A, Theorem A and the Section 4 injectivity argument; an explicit account (by the author or the v2 comment) of what changed between v1 and v2; a check of the algebraically closed reduction against the text; a statement from Schaub and Spivakovsky of what they checked; and, if any later paper engages with the argument, its verdict.
